## Historical audit: S0135

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/generic_rsi/C2/test/commons_199974832/trajectory.jsonl`. Only chunk 3 of 3 is available here; citations below refer to its JSONL observations.

| Evidence | Observation and limit |
|---|---|
| Student `model_request`, line 19, characters [0,306614) | The task was to reconstruct a 512×384 indoor photograph as separate editable meshes, matching viewpoint, occlusion and color. The student interpreted it as a woodworking tool room; that interpretation and its landmark estimates are not independent verification of the unseen photograph. |
| Same event, initial program | The code creates multiple assemblies: walls, window, shelves, bench, numerous planes and tools, and containers. It groups component meshes, including a solid bench top and apron, legs, plane bodies and open handles. Grouping and intended contacts do not establish physical connection, support, or correct pose. Wood noise and metallic shader settings are specified; their visual fidelity is unverified. |
| Same event, step 1 feedback and step 2 program | Step 1 reports `ok: true` and `render_available`. The student estimated shelf and bowl discrepancies, attributed pale surfaces to shader color handling, increased lens 31→36, extended walls to address an alleged sky band, and transferred diffuse colors to shader nodes. Camera, material and geometry changes were combined; illumination was retained. These are the student's observations and hypotheses, not independently checked image facts. |
| Same event, step 2 feedback and step 3 program | Step 2 also reports a render. The student judged framing close but surfaces still pale, then retained the camera and lighting while darkening the palette and assigning explicit materials using named primitives and parent traversal. This is an executed revision, not proof that the proposed material diagnosis was correct. |
| Same event, step 3 feedback; lines 20–22, characters [0,4276), [0,344), [0,58) | Step 3 reports `ok: true`, a saved render and no error. With no executions left, the selection-only request constrained further work. A read-only student session with no tool calls returned `SELECT 3`; the following `select` event records step 3. This establishes successful execution and selection, **not formal visual or geometric correctness**. |

**Teacher input and exploration.** The visible request contains system/API guidance and runner feedback, including prompts to compare renders and make narrow corrections. No separately identified teacher diagnosis, proposed update, or teacher-to-student receipt appears in this chunk; adoption of teacher-specific advice is therefore unknown. The student independently produced and revised programs in response to actual render availability, but the images themselves are not visible to this audit.

**Transfer and uncertainty.** The trace illustrates separating executable render success from reconstruction quality, and checking material assignment after realization. The particular lens, wall extension and palette are scene-specific hypotheses. Whether the selected render matches the reference in object coverage, part contacts, poses, framing, lighting or tone—and whether the alleged pale materials and sky band were fixed—remains unresolved. Other chunks may contain additional evidence; none is assumed here.
